findings_addressed.oracle: Bounded chunk count oracle: a prompt requesting 50 numbered lines would produce far more than 10 chunks if cancel were not honoured; asserting received <= _MAX_CHUNKS_AFTER_CANCEL (10) proves the _cancel_requested guard in _iter_anthropic_stream's async-for loop actually terminated iteration, not merely that the flag attribute was set.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In src/intellicrack/providers/anthropic.py lines 731-733, remove `if self._cancel_requested: break` so the stream loop never checks the flag; the test then fails because received exceeds _MAX_CHUNKS_AFTER_CANCEL.

findings_addressed.oracle: Bounded chunk count oracle: a prompt requesting 50 numbered lines would produce far more than 10 chunks if cancel were not honoured; asserting received <= _MAX_CHUNKS_AFTER_CANCEL (10) proves the _cancel_requested guard in _iter_grok_stream's async-for loop actually terminated iteration, not merely that the flag attribute was set.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In src/intellicrack/providers/grok.py lines 942-944, remove `if self._cancel_requested: break` so the stream loop never checks the flag; the test then fails because received exceeds _MAX_CHUNKS_AFTER_CANCEL.

notes: Both findings were tautological: the original tests called cancel_request() and immediately broke out of the loop via an explicit `break`, meaning the streaming loop's `if self._cancel_requested: break` guard was never exercised. The fix removes the manual break and instead lets the streaming loop's cancel check stop iteration naturally. The assertion received <= _MAX_CHUNKS_AFTER_CANCEL (10) serves as the independent oracle: a 50-item countdown without cancellation would produce far more chunks, so exceeding 10 proves the guard is absent or non-functional.
